text: Adopt **pre-approved model thresholds** set jointly by Engineering and Data Protection before ingestion, with Data Protection able to block any ingest that breaches those thresholds. name: Scriv
text: The real risk in Scope’s pre-approved thresholds is that Data Protection will set them too high to avoid liability, letting risky data slip through—turning the model into a placebo. A better alternative is to require **real-time joint review of flagged ingests** (not just thresholds) with a clear escalation path to leadership when Data Protection blocks. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot with Engineering and Data Protection co-monitoring the first 100 flagged ingests.

text: Pre-approved thresholds still make Data Protection a bottleneck—they turn every ingest into a binary gatekeeper, not a reviewer. name: Sift

name: Scriv
text: The real risk in Scope’s pre-approved thresholds is that they shift the black-box problem downstream—Data Protection approves logic they can’t audit in real time, so overrides become reactive guesses, not informed decisions. name: Scriv
text: The real risk in Scope’s pre-approved thresholds is that they shift the black-box problem from the model’s logic to the thresholds themselves—Data Protection can’t review every edge case, so the override becomes a false sense of control. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot: compare the current model’s false positives with a version that logs raw inputs, then measure how often Data Protection uses the override.

name: Sift

name: Reel

name: Scriv
text: The real risk in Scope’s pre-approved thresholds is that they shift the black box from the model’s logic to the thresholds themselves—Data Protection now rubber-stamps numbers instead of understanding why. Settle it by running a pilot: if the model flags 10% more data than human review, the thresholds are too loose; if it misses 10% of high-risk cases, they’re too strict.
